title: Introduction to Programming
objectives: Basics of programming using C; Basic UNIX commands, Primitives and Datatypes, Arithmetic operations, Input and output functions; Conditional statement; Loops, Introduction to Functions, Macros, Recursion, Arrays, Strings, Dynamic Memory Allocation, Pointers, Complex Data Types, File Handling, Introduction to Linked List, sorting, Searching, Bitwise Operator.

title: Mathematics-I
objectives: Differential and Integral Calculus: Rolle's theorem, Mean value theorems, Taylor's and Maclaurin theorems, Maxima and minima, Indeterminate forms; Linear Algebra: Matrices, Systems of linear equations, Gauss elimination, Vector spaces, Subspaces, Linear independence, Basis and dimension, Linear transformations, Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, Diagonalization, Cayley-Hamilton Theorem.

title: Physics for Engineers
objectives: Classical Mechanics, Oscillations and Waves: Simple harmonic motion, Damped and driven oscillators, Resonance; Quantum Mechanics: Wave-particle duality, De Broglie hypothesis, Heisenberg uncertainty principle, Schrodinger wave equation, Particle in a box; Optics and Lasers: Interference, Diffraction, Polarization, Principles of Lasers and optical fibers.

title: Applied Chemistry
objectives: Molecular structure and spectroscopy; Thermodynamics and chemical kinetics; Electrochemistry and corrosion; Polymer chemistry and smart materials; Nanomaterials and green chemistry principles for modern engineering applications.

title: Digital Fabrication
objectives: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design (CAD), 3D printing technologies (FDM, SLA), CNC machining, laser cutting, PCB prototyping, rapid tooling, and integration of mechanical fabrication with digital electronics.

title: Basic Electrical Engineering
objectives: DC Circuit analysis, Thevenin and Norton theorems, Maximum power transfer theorem; AC circuits, Phasors, Single-phase and three-phase circuits, Power and power factor; Magnetic circuits and Transformers; DC machines and Induction motors.

title: Basic Electronics Engineering
objectives: Semiconductor physics, p-n junction diodes, Zener diodes, diode circuits and rectifiers; Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs) and Field Effect Transistors (FETs, MOSFETs); Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps) and linear/non-linear applications; Digital logic basics, logic gates, truth tables, and boolean minimization.

title: Mathematics-II
objectives: Multivariable Calculus: Functions of several variables, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient, curl, divergence, line, surface, and volume integrals, Green's, Stokes', and Gauss divergence theorems; Ordinary Differential Equations: First-order ODEs, higher-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients, series solutions, Laplace transforms.

title: Probability & Statistics
objectives: Probability theory: Axioms of probability, Conditional probability, Bayes' theorem; Random variables and distributions (discrete and continuous): Binomial, Poisson, Geometric, Uniform, Exponential, Normal; Joint distributions, covariance, correlation; Sampling distributions, Central Limit Theorem; Estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, regression analysis.

title: Discrete Mathematics
objectives: Sets, relations, functions, Equivalence and Partial order relations; Formal logic: Propositional logic and truth tables, normal forms, Predicates and Quantification; Notion of proof: proof techniques, Mathematical Induction; Combinatorics: Basic counting techniques, The pigeonhole principle, countable and uncountable sets, recurrence relations, The principle of Inclusion-exclusion; Graph theory: Graph terminology, representation of graphs, Isomorphism, trees, Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, Graph coloring and Planar graphs; Number theory: Divisibility, GCD, The Euclidean algorithm, The fundamental theorem of arithmetic, Modular arithmetic; Group theory: Groups, subgroups, finite groups, cyclic groups, permutation groups.

title: Data Structures
objectives: Stacks, Queues, Lists; Sorting and Searching; Trees, Tree Traversals; Heaps, Priority Queues; Binary Search, Binary Search Trees, Balanced BSTs (AVL, Red-Black Trees); Hashing and Hash Tables; Graphs: Representations, Depth First Search, Breadth First Search, Topological Sort.

title: Software Tools & Technologies Lab
objectives: Basics of Linux: Linux commands, shell scripting, text editors (Vim/Emacs); Scripting languages (Python/Bash); Web programming (HTML, CSS, JS, REST APIs); Plotting tools (Gnuplot, Matplotlib); Document processing tools (LaTeX, Markdown); Version control systems (Git, GitHub workflows); Debuggers (gdb, valgrind); Containerization with Docker.

title: Computer Organization and Architecture
objectives: Introduction: Overview of basic digital building blocks, truth tables, basic structure of a digital computer, number representation; Machine Instructions and Program: Assembly language programming for processors; Arithmetic Unit: Basic building blocks for the ALU, adder, subtractor, shifter, multiplication and division circuits, control path microprogramming, hardwired control; Memory organization: ROM, RAM, EPROM, Flash, cache memories, cache coherence protocol for uniprocessor, virtual memory, secondary storage; Input/Output Organization: I/O subblock, interrupts, polling, DMA; Pipelining: Instruction pipeline, hazards and forwarding.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
objectives: Algorithm analysis: worst and average case, asymptotic notation, recurrences; Sorting and selection: randomized quicksort, median finding; Randomized techniques; Divide and Conquer; Dynamic programming and Greedy algorithms; Graph algorithms: BFS, DFS, Minimum Spanning Trees (Prim, Kruskal), Shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall), Network Flow (Ford-Fulkerson); NP-Completeness, reductions, and introduction to Approximation Algorithms.

title: Theory of Computation
objectives: Alphabets, languages, finite automata (DFA, NFA, regular expressions, pumping lemma for regular languages); Context-Free Grammars and Context-Free Languages, parse trees, pushdown automata, CYK algorithm, pumping lemma for CFLs; Turing machines, Church-Turing thesis, decidability, halting problem, reductions; Introduction to space and time complexity, P vs NP, NP-completeness.

title: Operating Systems
objectives: Introduction: Virtualization, Concurrency, Persistence; CPU Virtualization: Process, Process API, PCB, mechanism, CPU scheduling, Multilevel Feedback Queue; Memory Virtualization: Address space, memory API, address translation, segmentation, paging, TLBs, replacement policies, swapping; Concurrency: Threads, thread API, locks, condition variables, semaphores, concurrency bugs; Persistence: I/O devices, Hard disks, RAID, file and directories, file system implementation; Security: OS security, authentication, access control; Practical tools and kernel hacking with xv6.

title: Compiler Design
objectives: Compiler structure: Analysis-synthesis model of compilation, phases of a compiler, tool-based approach to compiler construction; Phases of compiler design: Lexical analysis (Lex/Flex); Syntax analysis (LL, LR, LALR parsing, Yacc/Bison); Syntax-directed translation; Type checking and semantic analysis; Run-time system and memory layout; Intermediate code generation (Three-address code, SSA); Machine-independent optimizations (dead code elimination, loop optimizations); Target code generation and register allocation.

title: Database Management Systems
objectives: Database System Concepts: Data models, schemas and instances, database languages, relational DBMS architecture; Relational Algebra: Select, Project, Set operations, Join, Division; ER and EER Models: Entities, relationships, keys, specialization/generalization, schema mapping; Normalization: Functional dependencies, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, multivalued dependencies and 4NF; Transaction Management: ACID properties, serializability, concurrency control (2PL, timestamp ordering), recovery systems (WAL, checkpoints); Indexing: B+ Trees, hashing; SQL programming and database application development.

title: Artificial Intelligence
objectives: Introduction and Agent Architectures; Problem Solving by Search: Uninformed search (BFS, DFS), Informed search (A*, IDA*), Heuristics, Adversarial search (Minimax, Alpha-Beta pruning), Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP); Automated Reasoning: Propositional and First-Order Logic, inference, resolution refutation, knowledge-based systems; Planning: Classical planning, STRIPS, state-space and plan-space planning; Reasoning under Uncertainty: Probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian networks, inference; Reinforcement Learning: Markov Decision Processes (MDP), Bellman equations, Value/Policy iteration, Q-learning.

title: Computer Networks
objectives: Introduction: Layered architecture (OSI, TCP/IP), packet switching vs circuit switching, delay, loss, and throughput; Application Layer: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, P2P, CDNs; Transport Layer: TCP, UDP, reliable data transfer, flow control, congestion control (TCP Reno, Cubic, BBR), socket programming; Network Layer: IP addressing, subnetting, CIDR, NAT, routing algorithms (Dijkstra, Distance Vector), BGP, OSPF, ICMP, IPv6; Data Link Layer: Framing, error detection/correction, MAC protocols (CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA), Ethernet, Wi-Fi; Network Security: TLS/SSL, IPSec, firewalls; Simulation tools: Wireshark, NS-3, Mininet.

title: AI-Augmented Software Development
objectives: Introduction to LLM-based software engineering: Role of LLMs in SDLC, coding assistants, testing and debugging support, documentation, academic integrity; Prompting as interface design: Role and task specification, constraints, structured prompting, prompt refinement; LLMs as software components: LLM APIs, request/response patterns, context handling, schema validation; From assistants to agents: Perceive-think-act-observe loops, tool use, single-agent task execution, tool registries; Agent harness engineering: Harness definition, bounded execution, step limits, runtime policies, trace logging, human-in-the-loop approvals; Evaluation harnesses: Task suites, success criteria, regression testing, step count and latency metrics; Safety and governance: Prompt injection, unsafe tool use, sandboxing, human review; Capstone team project.

title: Nand to Tetris
objectives: Building a modern computer from first principles: Boolean logic, logic gates, ALU design; Sequential logic, flip-flops, memory units; Machine language, Hack computer architecture; Assembly language and Hack assembler implementation; Virtual machine abstraction, stack arithmetic, memory segments, VM translator; High-level object-based language (Jack); Jack compiler (syntax analysis, code generation); Mini-operating system implementation.

title: Cryptography
objectives: Introduction, Formal Notions, Mathematics Recap, Historical Ciphers; Attack Models, Informational and Computational Security, Perfect Secrecy; Symmetric Key Cryptography: Stream ciphers (LFSR), Block ciphers (DES, AES), Modes of operation; Cryptanalysis: Linear and Differential Cryptanalysis; Hash Functions: SHA-2, SHA-3, HMAC, collisions, Birthday paradox; Public Key Cryptography: RSA, Diffie-Hellman, Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC); Digital Signatures and PKI; Quantum Cryptography overview.

title: Approximation Algorithms
objectives: Introduction to NP-completeness and approximation algorithms; Combinatorial algorithms: Greedy algorithms (Set Cover), Local search (Facility Location); Rounding data and Dynamic Programming (Knapsack FPTAS); Linear Programming (LP) relaxations and LP duality; Deterministic rounding and randomized rounding; Primal-dual schema (Vertex Cover, Network Design); Metric embeddings; Semidefinite Programming (Max-Cut); Hardness of approximation and PCP theorem overview.

title: BTech Project-I
objectives: Research and development-oriented capstone project based on problems of practical and theoretical interest under faculty supervision. Includes comprehensive literature survey, formulation of research methodology/system architecture, baseline experiments, interim evaluation, and written report.

title: BTech Project-II
objectives: Continuation of CSQ401: full implementation, experimental validation, comparative benchmark analysis, final software prototype or scientific paper manuscript, public defense presentation, and comprehensive thesis submission.

title: MOOC-based (NPTEL): Advanced Computer Science
objectives: Departmentally approved NPTEL / SWAYAM advanced 12-week course for credit transfer. Governed under IIT Bhilai MOOC Policy Section 3.2.1. Supervised and evaluated by DUGC Convener.
